title: The river as a poor man's West End
summary: Mrs. Brunies compares the riverfront to West End, with the toll, and Brunies recalls swimming and a girl diving off the shed.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: It was better. That was a poor man. The river was a poor man's west end. Because west end, they had to go out there in a trolley. And you had to pay toll to go out there. Yes. At Metairie. There was a lady, Miss Murphy. She was a toll keeper. And she, you had to pay her, I don't know whether it was two minutes, 15 cents, something like that, to go through. But we used to go in on the trolley. And the child would go out to West End. He used to lose his band. See, it was way out in the air, out in the water. Oh, yes. And then they used to get a table set where you take them. See, marvelous. But I want to tell you, the river was a poor man's west end. And everybody could have bought it. I was out there.

The kids go in swimming down there? Well, I mean, you take on a Sunday afternoon. Yes. All the families go out on the riverfront. And there was one girl named Bebe Harrison. She used to jump, I mean, dive off the shed. Run and dive off the top of the shed.
Into the river. Into the river. And then, you know, they had the back shore. And it used to go walk down, you see. And, of course, that's how all of those children were drowned, too.
